problem: Linear constrained MDPs are vulnerable to adversarial environments when losses and costs change over time.
approach: A primal-dual policy optimization algorithm using weighted LogSumExp softmax policies with periodic policy mixing and regularized dual updates to handle adversarial losses under full-information feedback and stochastic costs under bandit feedback.
contribution: First algorithm achieving sublinear regret and constraint violation bounds of O(K^3/4) for online finite-horizon adversarial linear CMDPs.

problem: Deploying machine learning models on resource-constrained IoT devices requires lightweight models with small memory footprints.
approach: A compression scheme for boosted decision tree ensembles that rewards feature and threshold reuse during training and uses an alternative memory layout.
contribution: Achieves 4-16x compression ratio compared to LightGBM models while maintaining same performance, enabling autonomous edge devices.

problem: Standard ML methods lack interpretability and identifiability, making them unsuitable for scientific applications requiring transparent optimization structures.
approach: Behavior Learning (BL) framework parameterizes compositional utility functions from intrinsically interpretable modular blocks, each representing a utility maximization problem.
contribution: Unifies predictive performance, interpretability, and identifiability with universal approximation guarantees and strong empirical performance on high-dimensional data.

problem: Existing deep generative models cannot estimate potential outcome distributions from observational data with desirable properties like Neyman-orthogonality and double robustness.
approach: Develops generative Neyman-orthogonal (doubly-robust) learners (GDR-learners) instantiated with conditional normalizing flows, GANs, VAEs, and diffusion models.
contribution: GDR-learners possess quasi-oracle efficiency and rate double robustness, achieving asymptotic optimality for estimating conditional distributions of potential outcomes.

problem: Direct dense convolution with complex kernels is computationally prohibitive on resource-limited devices, and existing approximations lack efficiency or cannot capture non-convex kernels.
approach: A differentiable kernel decomposition framework representing complex kernels using sparse kernel samples, with dedicated initialization for non-convex shapes and kernel-space interpolation.
contribution: Achieves higher fidelity than simulated annealing and lower cost than low-rank decompositions for mobile imaging and real-time rendering applications.

problem: Text embeddings face severe privacy risks from embedding inversion attacks, and existing differential privacy defenses apply uniform noise causing excessive utility degradation.
approach: SPARSE framework combines differentiable mask learning to identify privacy-sensitive dimensions and Mahalanobis mechanism applying elliptical noise calibrated by dimension sensitivity.
contribution: Consistently reduces privacy leakage across six datasets while achieving superior downstream performance compared to state-of-the-art DP methods.

problem: Large reasoning models face benchmark contamination where training data includes evaluation benchmarks, but contamination detection is easily evaded during training.
approach: Studies two contamination scenarios: SFT followed by GRPO training, and SFT with CoT on advanced LRMs, analyzing how RL training obscures detection signals.
contribution: Shows that GRPO and PPO-style RL methods can conceal contamination signals, and CoT SFT makes most detection methods perform near random guessing.

problem: Vanilla distribution matching distillation (DMD) suffers from convergence difficulties when scaling to large flow-based text-to-image models like SD 3.5 and FLUX.
approach: Proposes implicit distribution alignment (IDA) to constrain divergence and intra-segment guidance (ISG) to relocate timestep denoising importance, combined with a scaled VFM discriminator.
contribution: SenseFlow achieves superior distillation performance for both diffusion and flow-matching text-to-image models at scale, converging for SD 3.5 Large and FLUX.1 dev.

problem: Neuroscience traditionally fragments into specialized domains focusing on isolated modalities and brain regions, hindering development of a unified model of cognition.
approach: TRIBE combines pretrained text, audio, and video foundation model representations with a transformer to predict fMRI responses across modalities, cortical areas, and individuals.
contribution: Achieved first place in Algonauts 2025 brain encoding competition with significant margin, precisely modeling spatiotemporal fMRI responses to videos.

problem: Existing benchmarks fail to capture the fine-grained and long-horizon nature of authentic laboratory work, limiting evaluation of MLLMs on scientific experiment understanding.
approach: ExpVid benchmark curates experiment videos with three-level task hierarchy: fine-grained perception, procedural understanding, and scientific reasoning linking experiments to conclusions.
contribution: 3.6K condition sets across six tasks and domains with 20K fine-grained annotations reveal that MLLMs excel at coarse recognition but struggle with details and high-order reasoning.

problem: Inferring parameters of high-fidelity stochastic simulators is challenging when the simulator is computationally expensive.
approach: MF-(TS)NPE applies multifidelity approach using transfer learning to leverage inexpensive low-fidelity simulations to efficiently infer parameters of high-fidelity simulators.
contribution: Requires up to two orders of magnitude fewer high-fidelity simulations than current methods while showing comparable performance on benchmarks and neuroscience tasks.

problem: Enterprise software automation on complex platforms like Salesforce requires evaluating computer-use agents on realistic CRM workflows with diverse enterprise tasks.
approach: SCUBA benchmark contains 300 task instances from real user interviews spanning administrators, sales, and service agents, operating in Salesforce sandbox with fine-grained metrics.
contribution: Reveals huge performance gaps: open-source models have <5% success vs closed-source 39% zero-shot; demonstration-augmentation improves to 50% success.

problem: Dataset distillation for vision-language tasks requires large-scale training and joint optimization, limiting scalability and cross-architecture generalization.
approach: Learning-free dataset distillation framework using CLIP embeddings for image-text alignment, prototype extraction, and unCLIP decoder for image synthesis without optimization.
contribution: Consistently outperforms optimization-based distillation and subset selection, achieving state-of-the-art cross-architecture generalization without full-dataset training.

problem: Video generation and editing remain fragmented due to architectural limitations and data scarcity, unlike unified image generation/editing frameworks.
approach: EditVerse represents all modalities as unified token sequences with self-attention for in-context learning; includes 232K curated video editing samples for joint training.
contribution: State-of-the-art performance across image/video generation and editing, surpassing open-source and commercial models with emergent cross-modal abilities.

problem: Existing image generation benchmarks either focus on isolated tasks, cover narrow domains, or provide opaque scores without explaining failure modes.
approach: ImagenWorld provides 3.6K condition sets across six tasks/domains with 20K fine-grained human annotations tagging object-level and segment-level errors.
contribution: Comprehensive evaluation of 14 models reveals models struggle more in editing than generation, excel in artistic domains but struggle with symbolic/text-heavy content.

problem: Understanding when LLMs transition from memorization to generalization during pretraining on mixed-domain data remains unclear.
approach: Studies grokking in MoE LLM pretraining by analyzing expert pathway evolution from random and non-smooth to structured and transferable across samples.
contribution: First verification that grokking emerges in practical MoE pretraining; local data groups enter grokking asynchronously; pathways reveal memorization-to-generalization transition.

problem: Full-waveform inversion is limited by sensitivity to initial models; continuous representation FWI mitigates this but shows slower high-frequency convergence.
approach: Develops wave-based neural tangent kernel (NTK) framework extending standard NTK analysis to reveal non-constant eigenvalue decay behavior in FWI.
contribution: Proposes IG-FWI hybrid representation combining INR and multi-resolution grids achieving balanced robustness and high-frequency convergence improvements.

problem: Robotic agents under partial observability struggle with long-horizon tasks where key cues appear long before affecting decisions due to limited memory and context windows.
approach: ELMUR adds structured external memory embeddings per layer with bidirectional cross-attention and LRU-based memory replacement/blending to extend effective horizons.
contribution: Extends effective horizons up to 100,000x beyond attention window; achieves 100% success on T-Maze up to one million steps and doubles performance on sparse-reward manipulation.

problem: Accurate tumor analysis requires step-wise clinical reasoning from imaging findings to pathology conclusions, but existing methods lack traceability and reasoning transparency.
approach: TumorChain combines 3D imaging encoders and clinical text understanding with cross-modal alignment and iterative interleaved reasoning for step-aligned pathology predictions.
contribution: Demonstrates consistent gains in lesion detection, impression quality, and pathology classification through multimodal interleaved causal reasoning with improved traceability.

problem: Systematic understanding of popular open-source DPO datasets remains lacking, making it unclear how preferences are selected and how well they reflect human judgment.
approach: First comprehensive data-centric analysis using Magpie framework to annotate samples for task category, input quality, and preference reward without relying on human annotations.
contribution: Reveals structural and qualitative discrepancies in reward margins; curates UltraMix 30% smaller than best individual dataset while exceeding performance across key benchmarks.

problem: Tool planning with LLMs treats tools as isolated components and fails to leverage inherent tool dependencies, especially with incomplete dependency information.
approach: GTool constructs request-specific tool graphs to select tools efficiently, generates graph tokens for dependency information, and predicts missing dependencies.
contribution: Achieves 29.6% improvement over SOTA with lightweight 7B LLM backbone, seamlessly integrating with various LLM models without extensive retraining.

problem: Existing language-model approaches to RTL circuit representation ignore topological structure inherent in RTL circuits and dataflow graphs.
approach: TopoRTL decomposes RTL designs into register cones, constructs dual modalities with behavior-aware tokenizers, uses topology-aware positional encodings and contrastive learning.
contribution: Significantly outperforms existing methods by explicitly modeling topological differences across RTL circuits and preserving behavior information.

problem: Sparse autoencoders often recover only token-specific, noisy, or highly local concepts due to neglecting temporal structure of language.
approach: Temporal Sparse Autoencoders (T-SAEs) incorporate contrastive loss encouraging consistent activations of high-level features over adjacent tokens.
contribution: Recover smoother, more coherent semantic concepts without sacrificing reconstruction quality, exhibiting clear semantic structure without explicit semantic signal.

problem: Achieving both scalability and high predictive performance in linear classification remains a persistent challenge despite their advantages in interpretability.
approach: Proposes geometric discriminant analysis (GDA) framework for linear classifiers adjustable by geometric corrections under constraints, including centroid discriminant analysis (CDA).
contribution: CDA offers good scalability with quadratic time complexity lower than LDA while providing interpretable decision boundaries.

problem: Theoretical understanding of transformer in-context learning typically assumes fixed dependency structures, while real sequences exhibit flexible context-dependent relationships.
approach: Proposes framework using Markov chains with randomly sampled causal dependencies where transformers must infer token dependencies directly from examples.
contribution: Proves two-layer transformer can implement Bayesian Model Averaging for optimal causal structure inference; attention patterns directly reflect inferred structures.

problem: Class-pose decompositions create representations relative to arbitrary training-dependent canonicals, but real data exhibits unknown instance-specific symmetries.
approach: RECON introduces canonical orientation normalization via right-multiplication correction yielding natural data-aligned canonicalizations and test-time canonicalization layer.
contribution: Enables unsupervised instance-level pose discovery, out-of-distribution pose detection, and plug-and-play improvement of pre-trained models without retraining.

problem: While Transformers dominate LLMs, alternatives like xLSTM offer linear complexity but their scaling behavior relative to compute budgets remains unclear.
approach: Comparative investigation of xLSTM and Transformer scaling across model sizes (80M-7B) and training tokens (2B-2T), including optimal model size dependence on context length.
contribution: xLSTM models consistently Pareto-dominate Transformers, delivering lower cross-entropy loss for the same compute budget with favorable scaling behavior.

problem: Speculative decoding performance is fundamentally limited by the draft model capacity due to parameter gap between draft and target models.
approach: RepSpec combines structural re-parameterization with draft model training, introducing redundant linear structures merged during inference, plus hybrid training strategy.
contribution: Significantly improves accepted sequence length in speculative decoding over EAGLE while maintaining inference efficiency without adding inference cost.

problem: Machine unlearning leaves persistent fingerprints detectable in LLM behavior and representations, creating a new reverse-engineering vulnerability.
approach: Studies unlearning trace detection using supervised classifiers on prediction logits or textual outputs, analyzing traces in intermediate activations.
contribution: Unlearning traces detectable with over 90% accuracy even under forget-irrelevant inputs; larger LLMs exhibit stronger detectability, revealing measurement signatures in activation space.

problem: Coverage constraints in conditional robust optimization are sufficient but not necessary for robustness, leading to overly conservative decisions.
approach: Conformal Robustness Control (CRC) directly optimizes prediction set construction under explicit robustness constraints instead of coverage constraints.
contribution: Enables more efficient decisions without compromising robustness; provides theoretical guarantees on both robustness and optimality.

problem: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) becomes misspecified when the true reward function cannot be realized via the policy class, causing failure modes like preference reversal.
approach: Analyzes DPO as statistical estimation over reward functions; proposes AuxDPO introducing auxiliary variables in loss function to move toward RLHF solution.
contribution: AuxDPO mitigates misspecification in DPO with superior performance on bandit settings and LLM alignment tasks compared to vanilla DPO.

problem: Object referring models lack explainability and trustworthiness, treating it as direct prediction without reasoning or rejection of non-matching expressions.
approach: Rex-Thinker formulates referring as explicit CoT reasoning task identifying candidates and step-by-step assessing matches; trained on HumanRef-CoT with structured reasoning traces.
contribution: Achieves verifiable predictions linked to visual evidence through interpretable reasoning and learns to abstain when no object matches the expression.

problem: Optimal sliding window size for hybrid attention-RNN architectures remains unclear, with larger windows not improving long-context performance as expected.
approach: SWAX uses stochastically changing sliding window sizes during training with xLSTM linear RNN layers, forcing models to leverage both attention and memory.
contribution: Short window attention encourages better xLSTM memory training; stochastic windows significantly outperform regular window attention on both short and long-context problems.

problem: Theoretical understanding of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) training dynamics remains limited, with unclear convergence properties for overparameterized settings.
approach: Investigates two-layer KAN optimization where only first-layer coefficients are trained via gradient descent with sufficient network width.
contribution: Guarantees convergence to global minimum with m=O(n^2) hidden layer width, a significant O(n^6) polynomial improvement over two-layer ReLU networks.

problem: HDR video reconstruction from degraded LDR sequences with alternating exposures struggles with noise and blur in frames and lack of real-world paired data.
approach: DeAltHDR proposes flow-guided masked attention for inter-frame alignment and two-stage training on synthetic paired data with self-supervised fine-tuning on unlabeled real video.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods with controllable attention ratio for adaptive inference costs and practical deployment via self-supervised learning.

problem: Change point detection in dynamic multilayer networks remains challenging without established theoretical guarantees or confidence interval procedures.
approach: Proposes two-stage algorithm combining seeded binary segmentation with low-rank tensor estimation for dynamic multilayer random dot product graphs (D-MRDPGs).
contribution: First consistency results for change point localization in dynamic network data with limiting distributions under vanishing/non-vanishing jump regimes and data-driven confidence intervals.

problem: Existing Turing machine simulations by transformers require O(s(n)) CoT steps per simulated step, leading to impractical reasoning lengths.
approach: Proves any (t(n),s(n))-bounded multi-tape TM can be simulated by constant bit-size Transformer with optimal O(s(n)) context window and only O(s(n)^c) CoT steps per TM step.
contribution: Significantly reduces efficiency gap with sparse attention using fixed geometric offsets; shows c can be made arbitrarily small by increasing head-layer product.

problem: Fine-tuning and inference for LLMs is time-consuming and expensive due to large model sizes requiring efficient strategies for downstream tasks.
approach: GradPruner prunes layers of LLMs guided by gradients during early fine-tuning stages using Initial Gradient Information Accumulation Matrix (IGIA-Matrix) for layer importance.
contribution: Achieves 40% parameter reduction with only 0.99% accuracy decrease across medical, financial, and general benchmark tasks simultaneously improving training and inference efficiency.

problem: Transformer-based models show redundancy in blocks, but existing pruning methods like cosine similarity lack proper metrics for identifying which blocks to remove.
approach: Proposes entropy-based pruning strategy where entropy of hidden representations serves as metric for information richness within computation blocks.
contribution: Entropy-based pruning surpasses cosine similarity methods in reducing model size while preserving accuracy, offering more reliable criterion than geometric similarity for pruning.

problem: Deep neural networks in safety-critical applications are poorly calibrated and prone to overconfidence, but mechanisms for improving calibration remain unclear.
approach: Analyzes sharpness-aware minimization (SAM) showing it counteracts overconfidence by implicitly maximizing entropy of predictive distribution; proposes CSAM variant.
contribution: SAM and CSAM achieve consistently lower calibration errors than other approaches, with theoretical analysis connecting sharpness to calibration properties.
